newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian upper house may debate budget Feb 11.
newsitem.headline: Russian upper house may debate budget Feb 11.

text.p: Russia's upper house of parliament may debate the 1997 budget on February 11, the head of the chamber said on Thursday.

Federation Council Chairman Yegor Stroyev told a news conference after meeting President Boris Yeltsin that the budget would be discussed at its next session, which starts on February 11 and runs for several days.
A chamber spokeswoman said previously the budget would be discussed on February 12.
"As a result of extensive work in committees we are now ready to consider the budget," Stroyev said.
"I think it will be approved with a bit of difficulty, but approved."

He said some members of the chamber, which represents the governments of Russia's regions, had expressed concern whether the budget revenue projections were realistic and whether the plan could be met without extra unbudgeted spending.
The draft envisages a deficit of 3.5 percent of gross domestic product, by Russian calculations, on revenues of 434.4 trillion roubles and expenditure of 529.8 trillion roubles.
The State Duma lower house of parliament approved the draft at a fourth final reading on January 24. It then passes to the Federation Council for consideration.
It also requires approval by Yeltsin before becoming law.
